entries.text: Unlocking the Black Box: The Role of AI Explainability (XAI) and Interpretability

entries.title: k3d-research
entries.text: As AI models become more complex and their predictions more critical, the need to understand their decision-making processes has become paramount.7 This is the domain of Explainable AI (XAI), a research field dedicated to making AI systems more transparent and trustworthy.8 For K3D, this is a non-negotiable component. The platform must be able to answer not just

entries.title: k3d-research
entries.text: what the data shows, but why the data is structured that way.

entries.title: k3d-research
entries.text: The analysis points to post-hoc, model-agnostic methods as being most relevant for K3D, as they can be applied to complex, pre-trained models without requiring access to their internal architecture.8 A key technology in this area is SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations), a method rooted in game theory that can determine the contribution of each feature to a model's prediction.8 This allows for both local explanations of a single data point and global explanations of the entire model's behavior.22 In addition, the use of example-based and counterfactual explanations can be particularly intuitive for human users, providing explanations in a language they can understand.8

entries.title: k3d-research
entries.text: Interpreting the inner workings of Large Language Models (LLMs) presents a unique challenge due to their immense scale and complexity. A full-stack approach is required, which includes not only traditional XAI but also newer methods that delve into the "latent knowledge" within the model's layers, such as those that visualize neuron activations or attention heads.23 A particularly powerful technique for grounding explanations is Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), which enhances an LLM's response by retrieving relevant information from a specific, trusted knowledge corpus.24

entries.title: k3d-research
entries.text: A profound opportunity for K3D lies in transcending traditional XAI. Instead of providing a textual explanation in isolation, the platform can link the "why" to a visual anchor in the 3D space. For instance, an embodied agent could verbally explain the importance of a specific feature, while simultaneously highlighting the corresponding data points in the UMAP plot or projecting a graphical overlay of SHAP values. This creates a symbiotic relationship where the 3D visualization provides tangible context for the explanation, and the explanation provides meaning for the abstract data. This approach moves the user from passively viewing a visualization to actively and intuitively understanding it, directly addressing the core problem of abstract concepts being "poorly understood".16

entries.title: k3d-research
entries.text: Embodied Cognition: Integrating Embodied AI Agents

entries.title: k3d-research
entries.text: An embodied AI agent is an intelligent system with a visual or virtual body that can perceive, learn, and act within its environment.9 For K3D, these agents are not merely a cosmetic feature but a critical, central component of the user experience. They provide a natural, human-like interface to the otherwise cold and mathematical reality of high-dimensional data, acting as a conversational interpreter.

entries.title: k3d-research
entries.text: The effectiveness of these agents will be based on a "world model," which is an internal representation of the virtual environment that allows them to reason, plan, and understand user intentions.9 This model would encode not just the location of data points but also their properties, spatial relationships, and the dynamics of the environment.9 This capability would enable the agent to perform multi-step tasks autonomously and to respond to user queries with context-aware actions.

entries.title: k3d-research
entries.text: Furthermore, these agents will form the basis of a "human-in-the-loop" active learning system.9 The agents can guide users through the knowledge space, and in turn, their world model can be continuously refined by observing and interacting with human behavior. The success of K3D depends not just on technical accuracy but on user engagement and trust. Human beings willingly ascribe social awareness to computers and tend to find interactions with embodied agents more enjoyable and trustworthy.25 The embodied agent transforms a dry data analysis session into a collaborative conversation, providing a familiar and approachable guide to a potentially intimidating 3D environment.26

entries.title: k3d-research
entries.text: The Knowledge Environment: Spatial Computing and 3D User Interfaces

entries.title: k3d-research
entries.text: The underlying technology that hosts the K3D experience is spatial computing, a concept that extends beyond simple Virtual Reality (VR) or Augmented Reality (AR). Spatial computing is a holistic framework where digital and physical elements interact dynamically across multiple senses.27 For K3D, this means the system must not only display the 3D data but also understand the spatial relationships between data points and allow for gestural, natural interactions within that space.6

entries.title: k3d-research
entries.text: The benefits of 3D user interfaces are clear: enhanced user engagement, improved spatial understanding, and a more intuitive, natural form of interaction.6 However, these benefits must be weighed against significant challenges. The creation of complex 3D visualizations is more difficult and time-consuming, and the hardware requirements can be substantial.26 A more subtle but crucial problem is the risk of misinterpretation; human depth perception cues may be inconsistent in a virtual environment, leading to a distorted understanding of distances and relationships.2

entries.title: k3d-research
entries.text: The path to success for K3D lies in designing not just for immersion, but for tangibility. The goal is to make the abstract data feel physically present, something a user can "walk in" and manipulate with gestures and tools.6 This design paradigm reframes data analysis as an act of physical exploration. A user should not just view a cluster of points; they should feel as though they can reach out, select a data point, and pull up a data card with additional information.18 This transforms the user from a passive observer into an active protagonist within the knowledge space, a key factor for fostering collaboration and a sense of ownership over the insights gained.29

entries.title: k3d-research
entries.text: The Knowledge3D Architecture: A Blueprint for Development

entries.title: k3d-research
entries.text: To realize the K3D vision, a robust, modular, and extensible architecture is required. The following sections describe a high-level blueprint for the system, from data ingestion to the final user interaction loop.

entries.title: k3d-research
entries.text: The Data-to-Spatial Pipeline

entries.title: k3d-research
entries.text: The core of the K3D platform is a multi-stage pipeline that transforms raw, unstructured data into a navigable 3D spatial environment.

entries.title: k3d-research
entries.text: Raw Data to High-Dimensional Embeddings: The pipeline begins with the ingestion of diverse data, including text, images, and sensor outputs.11 This raw data must be converted into a unified, high-dimensional vector space. For text-based data, a sophisticated model like BERT is an excellent candidate, as it can create embeddings that differentiate between contextual meanings of the same word.11 This process is crucial for cleaning and standardizing data to make it manageable for a deep learning model.11

entries.title: k3d-research
entries.text: The Dimensionality Reduction Layer: This layer processes the high-dimensional vectors, projecting them into a lower-dimensional space. The analysis indicates that UMAP is the optimal primary method, chosen for its balance of local and global structure preservation and its computational efficiency.14 Other methods, such as PCA and t-SNE, can be implemented as user-selectable options for specific analytical needs.4

entries.title: k3d-research
entries.text: The Spatial Knowledge Representation Model: This is a crucial, project-specific component. The raw 3D point cloud generated by dimensionality reduction is not sufficient. The system must build a symbolic spatial index that preserves semantic relationships between data points, transcending simple geometric location.31 This index, which can be thought of as the system's "world model," will serve as the foundation for the embodied agent's reasoning and interaction capabilities.9

entries.text: The Agent-to-Knowledge Interaction Loop

entries.title: k3d-research
entries.text: The success of the K3D experience hinges on a fluid and intuitive interaction loop between the user and the embodied agent.

entries.title: k3d-research
entries.text: User Intent Recognition: The embodied agent, powered by a Large Language Model, will not rely solely on text input. It will be designed to process multi-modal input, including voice commands, gestures, and gaze tracking.6 For example, a user's verbal query ("What is this cluster?") could be paired with a gesture pointing to a specific group of data points in the 3D space.

entries.title: k3d-research
entries.text: Knowledge Graph and RAG Integration: To ensure the agent’s responses are accurate and grounded in reality, it will be integrated with a knowledge graph.1 It will use a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) system to retrieve specific, relevant information from the high-dimensional data corpus.24 This architecture prevents the agent from providing erroneous or "hallucinated" responses, thereby strengthening user trust.

It may verbally explain a concept while simultaneously highlighting the relevant data points, projecting a related 2D chart onto a virtual surface, or revealing an underlying knowledge structure. entries.text: A critical initial challenge identified by the analysis is the inaccessibility of the core k3d_node_schema.json.34 This file is fundamental to the project's data structure, and its absence means that a core element of the project is not yet defined. A crucial first step is to design a robust, flexible, and extensible data schema from first principles, incorporating concepts of spatial and propositional knowledge representation.31 This schema must be capable of handling not just data points but the semantic and spatial relationships between them.

entries.title: k3d-research
entries.text: The inherent limitations of 3D visualization also pose a significant challenge. The risk of misinterpretation due to poor depth perception and the overall complexity of creating and navigating a 3D environment must be addressed.26 The proposed solution is a layered user experience that combines the immersive 3D environment with familiar 2D interfaces, such as data panels and charts, and, most importantly, the constant, conversational guidance of the embodied agent.6

entries.title: k3d-research
entries.text: Finally, the computational demands of high-dimensional data reduction and high-fidelity 3D graphics are a significant hurdle.28 While UMAP is efficient, the real-time interaction with a large, complex dataset requires substantial processing power. The system must be designed with scalability in mind, leveraging modern GPU architectures and cloud-based processing.

entries.title: k3d-research
entries.text: Strategic Recommendations for Phased Development

entries.title: k3d-research
entries.text: To manage these challenges, a phased development approach is recommended, focusing on a Minimum Viable Product (MVP) that proves the core concept before scaling to a full-featured system.

entries.title: k3d-research
entries.text: Phase 1: The MVP - The Static Knowledge Graph. The initial focus should be on proving the data-to-spatial pipeline. The analysis suggests that a Unity-based MVP is the most strategic choice for this phase. Unity is known for its user-friendliness, extensive asset store, and rapid prototyping capabilities, making it ideal for a small team.35 The MVP would be a non-interactive, read-only visualization of a knowledge corpus, without the embodied agent. This would validate the core concept of transforming complex data into an understandable 3D spatial representation.

entries.title: k3d-research
entries.text: Phase 2: The Interactive Agent. Once the core visualization is stable, the embodied agent and interactive features can be developed. This phase involves integrating an LLM, developing the agent's "world model," and building out the conversational capabilities. This is a crucial step for increasing user engagement and trust.

entries.title: k3d-research
entries.text: Phase 3: The Collaborative Knowledge Habitat. The final phase involves the development of a fully-featured, multiplayer, and real-time collaborative environment.3 The analysis indicates that a transition to Unreal Engine may be beneficial at this stage for its cutting-edge graphics capabilities and scalability for large, complex environments.35 This phase would realize the full vision of K3D as a platform for remote collaboration and shared knowledge exploration.

entries.text: Conclusion: A Call to Action

entries.title: k3d-research
entries.text: The Knowledge3D project is a pioneering effort to create a new, more intuitive interface for knowledge itself, one that amplifies human intelligence rather than displacing it. The vision extends far beyond a simple data visualization tool to encompass a symbiotic relationship between high-dimensional data, embodied AI, and a spatial computing environment. The success of this endeavor depends on a strategic, phased approach that acknowledges and addresses the project's technical and cognitive challenges.

entries.title: k3d-research
entries.text: By following the proposed blueprint—starting with a robust, UMAP-based visualization MVP, then integrating a conversational embodied agent, and finally building out a fully collaborative knowledge habitat—the project can be realized. This approach will transform the abstract and poorly understood concepts of high-dimensional data into a tangible, navigable reality. The analysis concludes that K3D is not merely an incremental improvement on existing tools; it is a foundational step toward a new era of human-AI collaboration, where our innate ability to reason spatially is finally leveraged to unlock the full potential of complex information.

entries.text: Form ↔ Meaning** – every pixel, vector and API route clarifies an idea.

entries.title: DEV GUIDELINES
entries.text: Edge-first** – deliver static content when possible and only compute dynamically when necessary.

entries.title: DEV GUIDELINES

entries.text: "## 1.1. Purpose and Audience

entries.title: openai temporal agents cookbook
entries.text: This notebook provides a hands-on guide for building **temporally-aware knowledge graphs** and performing **multi-hop retrieval directly over those graphs**."

entries.title: openai temporal agents cookbook
entries.text: "**Temporally-aware knowledge graph (KG) construction**

entries.title: openai temporal agents cookbook
entries.text: … A key challenge in developing knowledge-driven AI systems is maintaining a database that stays current and relevant. While much attention is given to boosting retrieval accuracy with techniques like semantic similarity and re-ranking, this guide focuses on a fundamental—yet frequently overlooked—aspect: *systematically updating and validating your knowledge base as new data arrives*.

entries.title: openai temporal agents cookbook
entries.text: … No matter how advanced your retrieval algorithms are, their effectiveness is limited by the quality and freshness of your database. This cookbook demonstrates how to routinely validate and update knowledge graph entries as new data arrives, helping ensure that your knowledge base remains accurate and up to date."

entries.title: openai temporal agents cookbook
entries.text: "**Multi-hop retrieval using knowledge graphs**

entries.title: openai temporal agents cookbook
entries.text: … Learn how to combine OpenAI models (such as o3, o4-mini, GPT-4.1, and GPT-4.1-mini) with structured graph queries via tool calls, enabling the model to traverse your graph in multiple steps across entities and relationships.

entries.title: openai temporal agents cookbook
entries.text: … This method lets your system answer complex, multi-faceted questions that require reasoning over several linked facts, going well beyond what single-hop retrieval can accomplish."

entries.title: openai temporal agents cookbook
entries.text: "Inside, you'll discover:

entries.title: openai temporal agents cookbook
entries.text: Practical decision frameworks** for choosing models and prompting techniques at each stage

entries.title: openai temporal agents cookbook

entries.title: openai temporal agents cookbook
entries.text: "**Why make your knowledge graph temporal?**

entries.title: openai temporal agents cookbook
entries.text: … Traditional knowledge graphs treat facts as static, but real-world information evolves constantly. What was true last quarter may be outdated today, risking errors or misinformed decisions if the graph does not capture change over time. Temporal knowledge graphs allow you to precisely answer questions like “What was true on a given date?” or analyse how facts and relationships have shifted, ensuring decisions are always based on the most relevant context."

entries.title: openai temporal agents cookbook
entries.text: "**What is a Temporal Agent?**

entries.title: openai temporal agents cookbook
entries.text: … A Temporal Agent is a pipeline component that ingests raw data and produces time-stamped triplets for your knowledge graph. This enables precise time-based querying, timeline construction, trend analysis, and more."

entries.title: openai temporal agents cookbook
entries.text: "**How does the pipeline work?**

entries.title: openai temporal agents cookbook
entries.text: … The pipeline starts by semantically chunking your raw documents. These chunks are decomposed into statements ready for our Temporal Agent, which then creates time-aware triplets. An Invalidation Agent can then perform temporal validity checks, spotting and handling any statements that are invalidated by new statements that are incident on the graph."

entries.title: openai temporal agents cookbook
entries.text: "**Why use multi-step retrieval?**

entries.title: openai temporal agents cookbook
entries.text: … Direct, single-hop queries frequently miss salient facts distributed across a graph's topology. Multi-step (multi-hop) retrieval enables iterative traversal, following relationships and aggregating evidence across several hops. This methodology surfaces complex dependencies and latent connections that would remain hidden with one-shot lookups, providing more comprehensive and nuanced answers to sophisticated queries."

entries.title: openai temporal agents cookbook
entries.text: "**Planners**

entries.title: openai temporal agents cookbook
entries.text: … Planners orchestrate the retrieval process. *Task-orientated* planners decompose queries into concrete, sequential subtasks. *Hypothesis-orientated* planners, by contrast, propose claims to confirm, refute, or evolve. Choosing the optimal strategy depends on where the problem lies on the spectrum from deterministic reporting (well-defined paths) to exploratory research (open-ended inference)."

entries.title: openai temporal agents cookbook
entries.text: "**Tool Design Paradigms**

entries.title: openai temporal agents cookbook
entries.text: … Tool design spans a continuum: *Fixed tools* provide consistent, predictable outputs for specific queries (e.g., a service that always returns today’s weather for San Francisco). At the other end, *Free-form tools* offer broad flexibility, such as code execution or open-ended data retrieval. *Semi-structured tools* fall between these extremes, restricting certain actions while allowing tailored flexibility—specialized sub-agents are a typical example. Selecting the appropriate paradigm is a trade-off between control, adaptability, and complexity."

entries.title: openai temporal agents cookbook
entries.text: "**Evaluating Retrieval Systems**

entries.title: openai temporal agents cookbook
entries.text: … High-fidelity evaluation hinges on expert-curated “golden” answers, though these are costly and labor-intensive to produce. Automated judgments, such as those from LLMs or tool traces, can be quickly generated to supplement or pre-screen, but may lack the precision of human evaluation. As your system matures, transition towards leveraging real user feedback to measure and optimize retrieval quality in production.

entries.title: openai temporal agents cookbook
entries.text: … A proven workflow: Start with synthetic tests, benchmark on your curated human-annotated “golden” dataset, and iteratively refine using live user feedback and ratings."

entries.title: openai temporal agents cookbook
entries.text: "**Keep the graph lean**

entries.title: openai temporal agents cookbook
entries.text: … Established archival policies and assign numeric relevance scores to each edge (e.g., recency x trust x query-frequency). Automate the archival or sparsification of low-value nodes and edges, ensuring only the most critical and frequently accessed facts remain for rapid retrieval."

entries.title: openai temporal agents cookbook
entries.text: "**Parallelize the ingestion pipeline**

entries.title: openai temporal agents cookbook
entries.text: … Transition from a linear document → chunk → extraction → resolution pipeline to a staged, asynchronous architecture. Assign each processing phase its own queue and dedicated worker pool. Apply clustering or network-based batching for invalidation jobs to maximize efficiency. Batch external API requests (e.g., OpenAI) and database writes wherever possible. This design increases throughput, introduces backpressure for reliability, and allows you to scale each pipeline stage independently."

entries.title: openai temporal agents cookbook
entries.text: "**Integrate Robust Production Safeguards**

entries.title: openai temporal agents cookbook
entries.text: … Enforce rigorous output validation: standardise temporal fields (e.g., ISO-8601 date formatting), constrain entity types to your controlled vocabulary, and apply lightweight model-based sanity checks for output consistency. Employ structured logging with traceable identifiers and monitor real-time quality and performance metrics in real lime to proactively detect data drift, regressions, or pipeline anomalised before they impact downstream applications."

entries.text: Core Changes: Impact on Memory and Performance

entries.title: core changes impact
entries.text: This note captures the effects of two fundamental changes in K3D’s core:

entries.title: core changes impact
entries.text: Embedding data inside GLB bufferViews (vs. JSON extras/sidecars)

entries.title: core changes impact
entries.text: Adopting an RPN execution substrate for agent‑level numeric reasoning

entries.title: core changes impact
entries.text: The goal is to make tradeoffs explicit and guide where each approach should be used.

entries.title: core changes impact
entries.text: GLB BufferViews vs JSON Extras

entries.title: core changes impact
entries.text: Change: Embeddings and vectors are stored in binary `bufferView`s inside GLB (or data URI in glTF), and referenced in `primitive.extras.k3d` via indices (`vectorsView`, `embeddingsView`, `embeddingDims`). Previously, embeddings often traveled as JSON arrays inside `extras.k3d` or via a sidecar `.k3d`.

entries.title: core changes impact
entries.text: Why it helps:

entries.title: core changes impact
entries.text: Size: Binary floats store exactly 4 bytes per value; JSON floats typically cost ~5–12 bytes plus separators. For moderate dimensionality, JSON payloads are ~5× larger.

entries.title: core changes impact
entries.text: Parse time: GLB avoids JSON parsing of large numeric arrays; loaders can map binary directly to typed arrays.

entries.title: core changes impact
entries.text: Streamability: BufferViews scale better to large scenes and progressive loading.

entries.title: core changes impact
entries.text: Measured (synthetic, embeddings only):

entries.title: core changes impact
entries.text: Implication: For any non‑trivial embedding set, GLB bufferViews yield substantial memory and bandwidth reductions, and reduce parse/GC pressure in the viewer.

entries.title: core changes impact
entries.text: Recommendation:

entries.title: core changes impact
entries.text: Use GLB with bufferViews for positions and embeddings (current default).

entries.title: core changes impact
entries.text: Keep a lightweight `extras.k3d` index (ids, metadata, neighbors, indices to bufferViews).

entries.title: core changes impact
entries.text: RPN vs Direct Arithmetic

entries.title: core changes impact
entries.text: Change: Agent‑level numeric operations use an RPN (Reverse Polish Notation) stack machine (JS and Python) for deterministic, parse‑free execution. This unifies introspection and replay across environments.

entries.title: core changes impact
entries.text: Deterministic, stepwise execution with a small opcode set.

entries.title: core changes impact
entries.text: Easy to instrument and log (good for imitation learning and debugging).

entries.title: core changes impact
entries.text: Language‑portable (same behavior in JS and Python).

entries.title: core changes impact
entries.text: Cost: Throughput vs vectorized math. Micro‑benchmark (Python):

entries.title: core changes impact
entries.text: Interpretation:

entries.title: core changes impact
entries.text: RPN is ~10^3× slower than vectorized NumPy for bulk cosine computations. Accuracy is identical (floating‑point noise).

entries.title: core changes impact
entries.text: Recommendation:

entries.title: core changes impact
entries.text: Use RPN for agent decisions, explanation traces, and small compute steps where interpretability matters.

entries.title: core changes impact
entries.text: Use vectorized math (NumPy/TypedArrays/WebGPU) for large‑scale operations (clustering, batch similarity, layout).

entries.title: core changes impact
entries.text: Bottom Line

entries.title: core changes impact
entries.text: Data: Move large numeric tensors to GLB bufferViews — it’s smaller, faster, and future‑proof.

entries.title: core changes impact
entries.text: Compute: Use RPN for explainable, stepwise agent logic; reserve vectorized backends for heavy lifting.

entries.text: K3D: A Vision for a Standardized Spatial Knowledge Reality

entries.title: K3D Vision and Standardization
entries.text: Introduction

entries.title: K3D Vision and Standardization
entries.text: This document presents a comprehensive vision for the Knowledge3D (K3D) project, expanding on the core concepts of Fog Computing, the AI Avatar, the literal "House" memory palace, and the avatar "Cranium" (head) galaxy knowledge storage.

entries.title: K3D Vision and Standardization
entries.text: The K3D project's mission is to **make knowledge spatial, social, and sentient**. We believe that the current paradigm of flat, 2D linear or planar interfaces for interacting with information is a bottleneck to human-AI collaboration and unprecedented knowledge advances. By representing knowledge as a navigable, 3D representative universe (like any AAA modern game), we can unlock new modes of discovery, creativity, and understanding.

entries.title: K3D Vision and Standardization
entries.text: This report will detail the technical architecture that makes this vision possible, from the distributed fog computing infrastructure to the intimate, personal memory spaces of AI agents.

entries.title: K3D Vision and Standardization
entries.text: The K3D Vision: A Spatial Knowledge Reality

entries.title: K3D Vision and Standardization
entries.text: The "knowledgeverse" is a shared, persistent, 3D world environment where data, information, and knowledge are represented as objects in space. This is not merely a visualization; it is a new form of reality, where humans and AI can interact with knowledge as a tangible thing.

entries.title: K3D Vision and Standardization
entries.text: Key principles of the K3D vision include:

entries.title: K3D Vision and Standardization
entries.text: Internal Spatialization:** Every piece of knowledge, from a single data point to a complex concept, has a location and graphical representation in the 3D space (Galaxy of knowledge). The spatial relationships between these objects are meaningful, representing semantic similarity, causal links, or other connections.

entries.title: K3D Vision and Standardization
entries.text: Socialization:** The knowledgeverse is a multi-user game-like environment. Humans and AI avatars can explore the 3D spaces and addresses together, collaborating on tasks, using spatial software (like a BIM modelling software or an online paid RPG), sharing insights, and building new knowledge structures.

entries.title: K3D Vision and Standardization
entries.text: Sentience:** The knowledgeverse is not a static repository. It is a dynamic, living system, populated by AI avatars that can reason, learn, remember and act within the virtual earth-human-like environment.

entries.title: K3D Vision and Standardization
entries.text: The Fog Computing Architecture: A Distributed Foundation

entries.title: K3D Vision and Standardization
entries.text: To realize the K3D vision, we require a new kind of infrastructure that can support real-time, immersive experiences at a global scale. A centralized, cloud-only architecture would be insufficient, as it cannot provide the low latency and data locality required for seamless interaction.

entries.title: K3D Vision and Standardization
entries.text: We propose a **three-tiered fog computing architecture**:

entries.title: K3D Vision and Standardization
entries.text: Cloud Layer:** The global backbone of the K3D network. It is responsible for:

entries.title: K3D Vision and Standardization
entries.text: Large-scale data storage and archiving (Knowledge gardens).

entries.title: K3D Vision and Standardization
entries.text: Training of large AI models (AI University).

entries.title: K3D Vision and Standardization
entries.text: Global user authentication and identity management (OSI scheme).

entries.title: K3D Vision and Standardization
entries.text: Orchestration of the fog and edge layers.

entries.title: K3D Vision and Standardization
entries.text: Fog Layer:** A distributed network of regional and on-premise nodes. The fog layer is the heart of the K3D system, responsible for:

entries.title: K3D Vision and Standardization
entries.text: Hosting the local and wide "House" memory palaces of AI avatars (think of the house as the point of connection to outside networks, the AI agent connects to the user's house, the user's house can connect to the open wide space - the spatial web or "knowledgeverse").

entries.title: K3D Vision and Standardization
entries.text: Running the "Cognitive Logic" of AI avatars (can be on premises or a third-party paid device using open or local AIs).

entries.title: K3D Vision and Standardization
entries.text: Real-time synchronization of open wide space 3D scenes.

entries.title: K3D Vision and Standardization
entries.text: Caching of frequently accessed data from the cloud.

entries.title: K3D Vision and Standardization
entries.text: Edge Layer:** The user-facing layer, consisting of AR/VR headsets, computers, and mobile devices. The edge layer is responsible for:

entries.title: K3D Vision and Standardization
entries.text: Rendering the 3D environment.

entries.title: K3D Vision and Standardization
entries.text: Capturing user input and sensor data.

entries.title: K3D Vision and Standardization
entries.text: Connecting to the nearest fog node for low-latency interaction.

entries.title: K3D Vision and Standardization
entries.text: This architecture provides the ideal balance of centralized control and decentralized execution, enabling a truly responsive and scalable Spatial Knowledge Reality.

entries.title: K3D Vision and Standardization
entries.text: The AI Avatar, House, and Cranium: A New Model for AI Memory

entries.title: K3D Vision and Standardization
entries.text: In the K3D universe, AI is not a disembodied service in the cloud. It is a first-class citizen, an **AI Avatar** with its own presence, identity, and memory.

entries.title: K3D Vision and Standardization
entries.text: The memory two aspects of an AI avatar memory (comparable to nowdays blob files together) are its **"House"** (a literal 3D space assembled as a human house, with bed, bookshelfes, rooms, sofa, TV of projector - the AI is binded to this memory palace when exploring the web using it's virtual tablet), a personal, 3D memory palace that it can inhabit and explore, and it's internal **"Cranium"** 3D shaped embeddings (using the galaxy of knowledge representation - accessible for audition using a special debug window). The House is not just a data store; it is an extension of the AI's own mind, a spatial and visual representation of our world. Knowledge and experiences become something humans can relate to and reason with.

entries.title: K3D Vision and Standardization
entries.text: The House is a structured, persistent knowledge store that resides on a fog node. The Cranium is composed of several key components:

entries.title: K3D Vision and Standardization
entries.text: D Knowledge Graph:** A 3D galaxy graph database that stores the AI's semantic knowledge, representing entities, concepts, and their relationships with the high-dimensional embeddings of data embedded at its 3D vectors and nodes, enabling similarity search and other forms of spatial vector-based reasoning.

entries.title: K3D Vision and Standardization
entries.text: Introspect mode:** AI can "navigate its head" to do introspect reasoning.

entries.title: K3D Vision and Standardization
entries.text: The AI's **"Cranium"** runs on the same fog node as its House, allowing for low-latency access to short and long memory. This co-location of short and long memory is crucial for creating AI avatars that are truly responsive and intelligent.

entries.title: K3D Vision and Standardization
entries.text: Standardization for the Spatial Web

entries.title: K3D Vision and Standardization
entries.text: For the Spatial Web to flourish, we need open standards that allow for interoperability between different applications, devices, and AI systems. We propose that the K3D project serve as the foundation for these standards, and by doing so, we can create a vibrant ecosystem of interoperable tools and services for the Spatial Web, enabling humankind to discover unthinkable things.

entries.title: K3D Vision and Standardization
entries.text: Impact and Future Work

entries.title: K3D Vision and Standardization
entries.text: The K3D project has the potential to revolutionize a wide range of industries, from gaming and entertainment to education and scientific research. By making knowledge spatial, relatable, and sentient, we can create new possibilities for human-AI collaboration and collective intelligence.

entries.title: K3D Vision and Standardization
entries.text: We invite the community to join us in building the future of the Spatial Web.

entries.text: Facial Expression: Concentrated, with slightly furrowed brows and eyes narrowed in thought—like someone debugging a complex problem.

entries.text: Inner Galaxy: Through a translucent, glowing forehead (or skull-like structure), show the avatar’s internal galaxy: swirling nodes (representing embeddings) and luminous pathways (semantic connections). As the avatar processes the port address, highlight specific nodes lighting up (e.g., a “network protocol” node pulsing, or a “security” node shifting color) to indicate active cognition.

entries.title: avatar workshop prompt

entries.title: avatar workshop prompt
entries.text: Style: Photorealistic, with a balance of organic warmth (skin texture, natural shadows) and digital glow (inner galaxy, holograms). Emphasize the fusion of human and AI—e.g., the avatar’s skin has a faint, circuit-like pattern, or its eyes reflect the galaxy’s light.

entries.title: AI RPN standard
entries.text: AI Runtime: RPN Logic Standard

entries.title: AI RPN standard
entries.text: Overview

entries.title: AI RPN standard
entries.text: The internal AI control logic uses a small Reverse Polish Notation (RPN) core for deterministic, data‑parsimonius computation across clients.

entries.title: AI RPN standard
entries.text: RPN covers vector ops (dot, norm, cosine), scalars (+, -, *, /, abs, min, max), and simple stack machine flow.

entries.title: AI RPN standard
entries.text: Rationale

entries.title: AI RPN standard
entries.text: Determinism and auditability: tiny, testable operators make reasoning traces reliable.

entries.title: AI RPN standard
entries.text: Transport efficiency: instructions are compact and loggable.

entries.title: AI RPN standard
entries.text: Cross‑client parity: the same minimal core works in HR viewer and MR runtimes.

entries.title: AI RPN standard
entries.text: Reference Implementation

entries.title: AI RPN standard
entries.text: HR: `viewer/src/rpn.ts` provides the canonical stack machine used by `K3DAgent` for cosine similarity and mic processing.

entries.title: AI RPN standard
entries.text: MR: mirror this module when generating production builds via `codeopt`.

entries.title: AI RPN standard
entries.text: Integration Points

entries.title: AI RPN standard
entries.text: Agent navigation: cosine similarity between embeddings powers “per‑hop” explain traces.

entries.title: AI RPN standard
entries.text: Signal handling: simple DSP readouts (e.g., mic peak) rely on RPN ops.

entries.title: AI RPN standard
entries.text: Future: server‑side MR components can adopt the same operator set for consistency.

entries.title: AI RPN standard
entries.text: Spec Notes

entries.title: AI RPN standard
entries.text: RPN is a logic substrate, not a replacement for model inference. It standardizes local computations close to the data plane.

entries.title: AI RPN standard
entries.text: Operators MUST be pure and side‑effect free.

entries.title: glTF K3D extension
entries.text: glTF K3D Data (Draft)

entries.title: glTF K3D extension
entries.text: K3D supports two representations for aligning knowledge with 3D geometry:

entries.title: glTF K3D extension
entries.text: Legacy sidecar via `K3D_nodes` extension: a glTF scene links to an external `.k3d` JSON.

entries.title: glTF K3D extension
entries.text: Embedded variant: all K3D node data (IDs, vectors, embeddings, metadata) is stored directly in `primitive.extras.k3d`.

entries.title: glTF K3D extension
entries.text: Sidecar Properties (Legacy)

entries.title: glTF K3D extension
entries.text: | Property | Type | Description |

entries.title: glTF K3D extension
entries.text: | `uri` | string | Relative or absolute URI of the `.k3d` file containing node entries that follow `k3d_node_schema.json`. |

entries.title: glTF K3D extension
entries.text: | `schema` | string | Optional URI to a JSON schema describing the `.k3d` node format. Defaults to `k3d_node_schema.json` when omitted. |

entries.title: glTF K3D extension
entries.text: | `nodeProperty` | string | JSON pointer indicating where each glTF **node** stores a corresponding K3D `id`. For scenes with distinct objects. Defaults to `extras.k3dId`. |

entries.title: glTF K3D extension
entries.text: | `primitiveIdsProperty` | string | JSON pointer indicating where a mesh **primitive** stores a list of K3D `id`s. For point clouds or batched geometries. |

entries.title: glTF K3D extension
entries.text: Example (Point Cloud)

entries.title: glTF K3D extension
entries.text: Embedded Variant (Recommended)

entries.title: glTF K3D extension
entries.text: Data is embedded within the mesh primitive to keep geometry and semantics in a single asset.

entries.title: glTF K3D extension
entries.text: Location: `meshes[n].primitives[m].extras.k3d`

entries.title: glTF K3D extension
entries.text: Schema (informal):

entries.title: glTF K3D extension
entries.text: `vectorsView` is a `bufferView` index of packed Float32 triples (x,y,z for each node).

entries.title: glTF K3D extension
entries.text: `embeddingsView` is a `bufferView` index of packed Float32 embeddings concatenated row-wise; `embeddingDims` gives the per-node dimension.

entries.title: glTF K3D extension
entries.text: `embeddingPrecision`: optional, one of `"f32"|"f16"`. When `f16`, the embeddings bufferView stores IEEE754 half-precision floats (2 bytes); readers should decode to float32 for processing.

entries.title: glTF K3D extension
entries.text: `primitive.extras.k3dIds` mirrors the `ids` array for simple readers.

entries.title: glTF K3D extension
entries.text: AI-native optional fields

entries.title: glTF K3D extension
entries.text: `ai_interaction_protocol` (string): One of `direct_vector_manipulation`, `semantic_query`, or `spatial_reasoning`. Specifies how AI agents are expected to interact with this payload.

entries.title: glTF K3D extension
entries.text: `ai_state_flags` (object): Dynamic flags for AI runtime. Suggested keys: `is_active` (bool), `is_traversable` (bool), `has_new_information` (bool).

entries.title: glTF K3D extension
entries.text: `ai_state_flags_mask` (object): Optional per-node boolean masks with same length as `ids`. Currently defined key: `has_new_information: boolean[]`. When present, it overrides global `ai_state_flags.has_new_information` for coloring/alerts.

entries.title: glTF K3D extension
entries.text: For large per-node embeddings, an additional compact form may be present per node entry or for the whole set: `embedding_b64` with `{ data, dtype, dims, endianness }` for efficient transfer.

entries.title: glTF K3D extension
entries.text: Rationale

entries.title: glTF K3D extension
entries.text: Separating K3D metadata into a sidecar keeps the glTF payload small while

entries.title: glTF K3D extension
entries.text: allowing rich graph relationships defined in

entries.title: glTF K3D extension
entries.text: [`k3d_node_schema.json`](k3d_node_schema.json).

entries.title: glTF K3D extension
entries.text: Compatibility

entries.title: glTF K3D extension
entries.text: Readers that ignore `K3D_nodes` or the `extras.k3d` payload continue to operate on standard glTF content. The embedded payload uses `extras` and remains valid glTF 2.0.

entries.title: k3d agent protocol
entries.text: K3D Agent Protocol (Extras)

entries.title: k3d agent protocol
entries.text: Location: `meshes[*].primitives[*].extras.k3d`

entries.title: k3d agent protocol
entries.text: Core fields

entries.title: k3d agent protocol
entries.text: `ids: string[]` — Node identifiers (aligned with vectors/embeddings order)

entries.title: k3d agent protocol
entries.text: `vectorsView: number` — BufferView index for Float32 POSITIONs (3D)

entries.title: k3d agent protocol
entries.text: `embeddingsView: number` — BufferView index for embeddings (Float32 or Float16)

entries.title: k3d agent protocol
entries.text: `embeddingDims: number` — Embedding width (e.g., 384)

entries.title: k3d agent protocol
entries.text: `embeddingPrecision: "f32" | "f16"`

entries.title: k3d agent protocol
entries.text: `metadata: Array<object>` — Per-node metadata; `metadata[i].label` is friendly text; `metadata[i].type` may be `"door"`

entries.title: k3d agent protocol
entries.text: `neighbors: string[][]` — K nearest neighbors per node, as node ids

entries.title: k3d agent protocol
entries.text: AI fields

entries.title: k3d agent protocol
entries.text: `ai_interaction_protocol: string`

entries.title: k3d agent protocol
entries.text: `"direct_vector_manipulation"` — Agent can write/update vectors/embeddings

entries.title: k3d agent protocol
entries.text: `"semantic_query"` — Agent queries only; no writes

entries.title: k3d agent protocol
entries.text: `"spatial_reasoning"` — Agent traverses/derives paths; read-only by default

entries.title: k3d agent protocol
entries.text: `ai_state_flags: { is_active?: boolean; is_traversable?: boolean; has_new_information?: boolean }`

entries.title: k3d agent protocol
entries.text: Global hints for the primitive

entries.title: k3d agent protocol
entries.text: `ai_state_flags_mask: { has_new_information?: boolean[] }`

entries.title: k3d agent protocol
entries.text: Per-node boolean mask for guidance; `true` marks points with newly available information

entries.title: k3d agent protocol
entries.text: Behavioral guidance (suggested)

entries.title: k3d agent protocol
entries.text: Path planning: use neighbor lists to route between labels; report cosine similarities per hop

entries.title: k3d agent protocol
entries.text: Exploration: prefer `has_new_information == true` when present; treat `metadata.type == "door"` as an anchor point

entries.title: k3d agent protocol
entries.text: Safety: refrain from writes unless protocol allows; honor `is_traversable == false`
